sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the opening header and date for the maamar.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
On the eve of Monday, Parshat Chayei Sarah,
the 20th of MarCheshvan, 5746

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the allegory of the woman crying to Elisha, identifying the soul as the woman, her husband as the lost love of G-d, the creditor as the animal soul, and the flask of oil as the essence of the soul.

translations.translation: "And a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, etc."
It is known from the discourse of the Alter Rebbe on the verse,
that "woman" refers to the soul,
and it is called "one woman" because it is one with Havayah,
"of the wives of the sons of the prophets,"
for "prophets" is from the term "utterance of the lips,"
meaning they receive from the aspect of "the word of Havayah," and the soul is a vessel to receive perceptions and revelations of G-dliness.
And "Elisha" is the letters of "Eli Sha," which is the Holy One, blessed be He.
And this is: "And a certain woman... cried out to Elisha,"
that the soul cries out to the Holy One, blessed be He,
"Your servant, my husband, is dead."
"My husband" is "Eish" (fire) and Yud,
for the love that was like "flames of fire" that I had, to be included and nullified in the aspect of the Yud of Supernal Chochmah—is dead,
meaning that now I do not have this love.
"And the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."
"And the creditor," from the term "for G-d has made me forget,"
refers to the animal soul, which causes me to forget G-dliness,
and "my two children" are love and fear.
[As explained in Tanya,
that the emotions are called "offspring,"
and the primary emotions are love and fear],
and this is: "And the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves,"
to [become] foreign loves and foreign fears.
[For in addition to the animal soul causing me to forget G-dliness and wanting, G-d forbid, to nullify the love and fear of G-dliness,
it wants to take the love and fear of the G-dly soul to be slaves to the animal soul].
"And Elisha said to her, 'What do you have in the house?'"
What powers remain with you over which the animal soul has no control?
"And she said, 'Your maidservant has nothing... except a flask of oil.'"
That nothing remained with her except the essential point of the soul.
[It can be said,
that "oil" is Chochmah,
and "a flask of oil" is the aspect of Chochmah within the soul,
over which the animal soul has no control].
"And he said, 'Go, borrow vessels for yourself from outside... empty vessels, do not make few.'"
That you should engage in Torah and mitzvos,
which are vessels for the light of Havayah,
and even though the Torah and mitzvos you are now engaged in are empty vessels
(without love and fear),
nevertheless, "do not make few" of them,
"and you shall pour [oil] upon all these vessels,"
to draw into them the revelation of the essence of the soul.
[In the manner explained in Tanya,
that the fulfillment of the Torah and its mitzvos depends on this, that one always remember the matter of self-sacrifice to G-d,
for self-sacrifice is from the aspect of the essence of the soul].
"And when you do this, then you and your sons shall live on the remainder,"
like the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness.
And there is another interpretation of "empty vessels, do not make few,"
that one should contemplate greatly
how he is an empty vessel, without knowledge in the brain and without awe and love,
and he should become very bitter over his distance,
and through this, the light of the soul will shine within him.
And as the saying of the Head of the Academy in the Garden of Eden:
"Wood in which no light shines, they strike it... a body in which the light of the soul does not shine, they strike it and light shines in it."
And moreover, this light
(that shines through the bitterness of being an empty vessel)
has an advantage over the light as it is in itself,
specifically like the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness.
And this is: "And you and your sons shall live on the remainder,"
"you" is the essence of the soul, and "your sons" are the awe and love within each soul—"shall live on the remainder,"
like the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the advantage of light from darkness achieved through bitter contemplation of being empty is superior to that achieved through performing mitzvos without love and fear.

translations.translation: It can be said,
that the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness
("and you and your sons shall live on the remainder")
according to the interpretation of "empty vessels, do not make few" that one should contemplate greatly how he is an empty vessel,
is more elevated than the advantage of the light
("remainder")
according to the interpretation of "empty vessels, do not make few" that one should engage in Torah and mitzvos even though they are without love and fear.
For behold, regarding the advantage of light from darkness,
there are two matters.
[First,] the advantage of the light in order to illuminate the darkness.
That in order to illuminate a very distant and dark place,
a very great light is needed.
For so it is also regarding the advantage
("shall live on the remainder")
that comes through engaging in Torah and mitzvos without love and fear,
for this—that he engages in Torah and mitzvos even though he has no love and fear—
is because of the intensity of his connection to G-dliness from the aspect of the essence of the soul,
which is above the revealed faculties.
And there is another matter regarding the advantage of light from darkness,
that through the bitterness over the darkness that conceals His infinite light,
there is drawn forth from the aspect of "He made darkness His hiding place,"
a darkness that is above light
(above even a great light that illuminates even in the darkest place).
And this is the advantage
("shall live on the remainder")
that comes through contemplating how he is an empty vessel,
for through the bitterness over being an empty vessel
(darkness),
he reaches the aspect of darkness that is above light.
